Name: Anna Cummins
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

I think visual texts like the slideshow will benefit my 7th graders because the annotation process might be too rigorous. I would love to do the annotation versions with my 8th graders. I think they will be able to handle the challenge next semester.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I can see myself using photos from the Holocaust and WWII to intoduce the literature circles I'm going to use with my 8th graders.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I think when looking at text so deeply and with detail, things like "main idea" might be hard to identify when finished annotating. It will be important for students to be able to synthesize at the end.
